item.content:encoded:
This makes me think alot about how tragic Bright's existance actually is. I mean, watching your family (okay, maybe not family since half of the Bright family is immortal or at least has post-human lifespan), loved ones and friends die one by one while you are just unable to must be a horrible experiance.
That's probably why he became so detached too. Like, why would you try to get attached to anything, knowing it'll cease existing way before you.
I can practically imagine Jack Bright just completly loosing it one day and triggering an XK-class scenario.

item.title: (no title)
item.content:encoded:
It does really show that death is what gives life meaning. Bright is such a terrible person because he knows life will never end for him he will always be there, somehow.

It's.. kind of depressing when you think about it. Before his curse he was literally the most average person ever, now, he's a vengeful immortal who is a terrible person and holds no regard for human life because he's died so many thousands of times before.

item.content:encoded:
I liked this story because even though I knew about Bright and how he was trapped in a amulet and what not I just never really thought about it too much I just took it for it's face value but this put a somewhat pain in my chest and water in my eyes thinking about how Bright will live in practical immortality until an XK-event or until he finally loses it and is placed in some shit hole to rot till some unlucky agent stumbles upon it.

I think if more stories were written about the higher ups that most look at and just deem "crazy" or "op" and throw in the other side of how THEY suffer then it'd certainly bring to light how YES these people are crazy, and YES they've done some unspeakable things but for what? for humanity! At Least that's what I think at least.

item.title: (no title)
item.content:encoded: It's not something that would really fit in the article for 963, but you've worked it into the Foundation Tales well enough. Yet another aspect of 963 that plays up the "curse of immortality" angle. That said, it's possible that the Foundation doesn't know about that property of 963, and might decide to try sealing it away to punish Dr. Bright, but in the end that would only be a temporary setback, and he'd probably be more than a little annoyed with them for turning on him like that. In fact, the possibility of the current or future Foundation having to deal with an angry immortal that knows as much about them as Dr. Bright does may be part of why the Foundation gives him so much leeway.
